requirements.evidence: Every contract item is present: Queues properties/methods and view data (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:22-69, 101-254), Serve state and callNext (app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:22-58), both routes (routes/web.php:59-60), tabs (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:66-82; resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:5-99) and all required lang keys in both locales. The one missed detail is the task's requirement that interactive controls have aria-labels: the create, save, rename, deactivate/reactivate and access buttons in resources/views/livewire/entity/queues.blade.php:10,44-45,75-76,84,87,89 rely only on visible text.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through the existing actions (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:107,176,215,263; app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:93), validation uses #[Validate] (Queues.php:29,57; Serve.php:46), authorization goes through policies (Queues.php:73,124,152,172,197,213,226,259) and Blade x-label/x-input components are reused. Deviations: validateOnly() is used instead of the documented $this->validate() pattern (Queues.php:104,173; Serve.php:75), and public UI-state methods skip authorization (Queues.php:91-95,159-163,202-205,232-235).

security.evidence: Strong points: all client ids are resolved entity-scoped with findOrFail (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:261,271; app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:83), server-only ids are #[Locked] (Queues.php:23; Serve.php:34,52), every write action authorizes (Queues.php:124,152,172,197,213,226,259; Serve.php:93) and callNext is rate-limited (Serve.php:86). Gap: Queues::render() (Queues.php:286-302) exposes $memberships/$accessGrants from the client-writable managingAccess/accessQueueId without re-checking manageAccess, so a manager demoted after mount can still read the access list until a reload.

tests.evidence: Broad Pest coverage of the task: tests/Feature/Entity/QueuesTest.php covers create, duplicate slug, rename, toggle confirmation, access grant/revoke, foreign ids, tampered access ids and demotion; tests/Feature/Entity/ServeTest.php covers default selection, call order, mode filtering, the 30-ticket limit, channel translation, foreign queues, inactive/no-waiting, unauthorized calls, the locked property, invalid mode and rate limiting; tests/Feature/Entity/QueueNavigationTest.php and the members-tab tests cover routes/nav/tabs. Only a nit remains: the grantAccess/revokeAccess write path has no post-demotion unauthorized test (tests/Feature/Entity/QueuesTest.php:358-375).

simplicity.evidence: Reuses the four existing actions and x-label/x-input components and introduces no speculative service or repository layer. Queues::render() always loads every membership (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:302) even when the access modal is closed, and the three modal shells repeat some boilerplate, but the implementation is otherwise direct.

readability.evidence: Methods are small, clearly named and docblocked (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:71-127,169-183,269-275; app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:116-147), the views are structured with consistent Bulma classes and all visible text comes from lang keys (resources/views/livewire/entity/queues.blade.php, serve.blade.php).

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: the two Livewire components and views, the members tabs, navbar entries, routes, lang files, tests and the CHANGELOG entry (CHANGELOG.md:9-11). No unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: The task requires aria-labels on interactive controls, but the create, save, rename, deactivate/reactivate and access buttons are named only by their visible text and have no aria-label.

render() builds accessQueue/accessGrants from the client-writable managingAccess/accessQueueId without re-checking manageAccess, so a manager demoted after mount can still read the access list until a reload, even though the write actions are correctly authorized.
These actions use $this->validateOnly() rather than the project's documented #[Validate] + $this->validate() pattern, although validation still runs server-side.

closeCreate(), cancelRename(), cancelToggle() and closeAccess() are public Livewire endpoints that skip $this->authorize(), contrary to the convention that every public action authorizes, though they only reset view state.
The demotion test exercises openAccess() but not grantAccess()/revokeAccess(), so the setAccess() authorization path has no unauthorized-call test even though the conventions require one per action.
render() eagerly loads every membership even when the access modal is closed, adding a query to every Livewire update on the queues page.

review.summary: The change delivers the queues and serve pages, members tabs, navbar links, both locales and a strong Pest suite, reusing the existing actions and entity-scoped lookups. It is close to the task; the main gaps are the missing aria-labels on several queues controls and a render path that exposes access data after a demotion, plus a few convention and test nits, so I would approve it after minor fixes.
